blocks.heading: Stops Working Once You Have a Job

items.text: Two numbers explain why.
Read together, those numbers say the same thing: an open-ended, unpaid, unstructured plan is the least likely one to survive contact with a real job.

blocks.heading: India's Online Learning Landscape for Working Professionals

items.text: India now has one of the largest online-learning bases in the world, and the platform mix has matured well beyond generic MOOCs.
A joint initiative of the IITs and IISc offering thousands of free, faculty-led courses across engineering, science, humanities, and management, in 4, 8, or 12-week formats.
Global reach through university and company partners (Google, IBM, Stanford, and others), with Professional Certificates, Specializations, and full online degrees.

blocks.heading: Self-Study Plan That Survives a 9-To-6 Job

items.text: A study plan that assumes you have the free time of a student will fail against a real job within two weeks - roughly half of all course dropouts happen in that exact window.
Protect your best 45-90 minutes, not your leftover time
Identify the window where your energy is genuinely highest - often early morning before work, or a lunch-hour block - and defend it as fixed, non-negotiable time.
Free is not automatically worse, and paid is not automatically better - but they solve different problems, and treating them the same is how people either waste money or waste months.

Paid, structured courses buy you three things free content usually cannot: a syllabus someone already tested for logical order, a deadline that creates real accountability, and often a recognised name on the certificate.
A practical sequence: use free resources for the first two to four weeks to confirm genuine interest and rule out a wrong guess cheaply.

blocks.heading: Employers Actually Read Online Certifications Versus Degrees

items.text: This is the part most upskilling advice glosses over, and it genuinely varies by employer and role.

Second, that shift is uneven: broader surveys of employer attitudes have found Indian employers still lean more heavily on formal degrees as a hiring filter than employers in markets like the US, where skills-first hiring has moved faster.
The practical read for you: do not expect a certificate alone, from any platform, to substitute for a degree at companies that formally screen on education.

blocks.heading: Turning Course Completion Into Interview-Ready Proof

items.text: Show it: Do not stop at the course's built-in assignments.
Say it: Write a short case note for every project - what the problem was, what you tried, what you decided, and why.
Get it checked: Wherever realistic, connect the project to a measurable outcome - time saved, an error caught, a decision it informed, even for an unpaid or personal project.

blocks.heading: Way to a Real Skill Switch

items.text: Enrolling in three courses at once.
Buying the most expensive option to force commitment.
Collecting certificates instead of building proof.
Copying someone else's study schedule.
Treating the first stumble as proof it won't work.
